learningObjectives: Differentiate unit, integration, and end-to-end testing approaches.
Identify suitable tests for frontend and backend components.
Apply testing strategies to validate full stack application behavior.

activities.title: Testing Pyramid
activities.instruction: Explore the levels of the testing pyramid and what each level validates.

content.concept: Unit tests focus on small isolated pieces of logic, integration tests verify interactions between components, and end-to-end tests validate complete user journeys. The testing pyramid generally emphasizes more focused tests and fewer broad end-to-end tests.

descriptions: Test small units of logic in isolation, such as a validation function or utility.
Test multiple connected parts working together, such as an API route and database layer.
Test a complete user journey through the application, such as signing in and completing a purchase.

activities.title: Test Type Match
activities.instruction: Choose the test type that best fits the scenario.

content.concept: The appropriate test depends on the scope of behavior being verified: isolated logic suggests unit testing, connected components suggest integration testing, and complete workflows suggest end-to-end testing.

activities.title: Test Execution Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the stages of a typical automated test workflow.

content.concept: A test workflow defines what should be verified, prepares the required environment or data, executes the test, evaluates the result, and reports failures for investigation.

activities.title: Test Suite Builder
activities.instruction: Build a balanced test strategy for a full stack feature.

content.concept: A full stack feature can require multiple testing layers: isolated logic tests, integration tests for connected systems, and end-to-end tests for critical user journeys.
